messages:
rachel: Hi team, first-day laptop drama  Windows booted into a BitLocker recovery screen after an overnight update. It wants a recovery key. Intune shows the device as not enrolled and Azure AD join failed during setup. Who do I ping for the BitLocker key and re-enroll help?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @rachel! :tada: IT handles BitLocker/Intune re-enrolls. Pinging them now.
it-support: Hey Rachel  sorry you're hitting this on day one. Can you SMB paste the outputs of these (copy/paste is fine):
`manage-bde -status C:`
`dsregcmd /status`
`winver`
And did this machine get restored from an image or cloned disk?
rachel: Pasted outputs from the recovery console after I got back in with a temporary USB key (I had to boot recovery to get a shell):
`C:\> manage-bde -status C:`
`Volume C: [OS]`
`Size: 476 GB`
`Conversion Status: Fully Encrypted`
`Percentage Encrypted: 100.0%`
`Encryption Method: XTS-AES 128`
`Key Protectors:`
`Numerical Password`

`C:\> dsregcmd /status`
`+ Device state: Not AzureAdJoined`
`+ Workplace joined: No`

`C:\> winver`
`Windows 11 Pro 22H2`

I did accept a vendor migration to copy over my files from a personal drive earlier this week, might have cloned a partition.

it-support: Thanks  cloning is often why TPM PCRs don't match and BitLocker asks for the recovery key. Two things we can do: (1) pull the recovery key from your Azure AD device registration if it exists, or (2) clear the TPM and re-enroll the device into Intune/Azure AD so BitLocker can be re-provisioned. We usually try to find the key first to avoid data loss.
jamie: @rachel I can grant a 60-minute temp-admin session so we can run the recovery retrieval flow and rejoin. I'll DM you. Also @it-support can you check Azure AD for any existing device objects matching her serial or device name?
it-support: On it. @people-ops can you confirm Rachel's Azure AD account is provisioned with the right role to view device keys or should we escalate to sam-security?
people-ops: Confirmed account exists but device-key lookup requires device admin or security team. @sam-security is on this thread now.
sam-security: We found a device object with a matching serial but no BitLocker key uploaded (likely because the device never successfully AzureAD-joined). Jamie, temp-admin session is fine. If we need to clear TPM, we will coordinate to avoid losing keys.
jamie: Temp-admin granted (60m). @rachel, please plug in your machine, I'll remote in and run `dsregcmd /join` and the Intune sync, then trigger an MDM policy to reprovision BitLocker protectors. If that fails we'll back up any user data and clear TPM then re-enable BitLocker under supervision.
rachel: Remote session started. Thanks! One quick question  will clearing TPM wipe user data?
jamie: Clearing TPM can invalidate the key protectors and cause data loss if you don't have the recovery key. We first attempt to recover key or rejoin without clearing. If we must clear TPM, we'll export any files you need to an encrypted company share before proceeding.
it-support: After joining, run `dsregcmd /status` to confirm AzureAdJoined: YES and then in an elevated prompt `gpupdate /force` and trigger the Intune sync (`Sync Device` from the Company Portal or `Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Intune\SyncApp.exe'` if present).
jamie: Update: rejoin succeeded, Intune device object created, pushing BitLocker policy now. Please reboot.
rachel: Rebooted, got a prompt to set up Windows Hello and BitLocker key protector automatically. No recovery screen. Phew.
sam-security: Verified a new BitLocker key is escrowed to Azure AD. I added a note to Rachel's device record about the earlier clone so future restores are aware.
people-ops: Welcome aboard again @rachel :wave: Let us know if you need any files recovered from the personal drive migration; we can coordinate with IT.
rachel: All good now  can access corp VPN and SSO. Thanks everyone for the quick help and the warm welcome :smile:
